clue.text: Recover — others grind to a halt

parts.note: to recover consciousness is to come to
the rest means the others, those remaining

explanation.surface: Someone recovering while everyone else around them grinds to a standstill.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to rest is to stop moving altogether, which is what grinding to a halt describes.

clue.text: Maybe eight die

definitions.meaning: eight is two multiplied by itself three times, a number of this cubic kind
a gaming die is a six-faced solid of this shape

explanation.definitionFit: Eight is an example of a perfect third power, and a die is an example of the six-sided solid shape.

clue.text: Intend having one's appearance mentioned

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word is heard rather than read on the page

parts.note: mien is a person's look or bearing

explanation.surface: Someone intending to have their looks talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to intend it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Start to dance, and to speak

definitions.meaning: couples step onto the dance area to begin dancing
in a debate one rises and is given the right to address the meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both going onto the dance area and rising to address a chamber or meeting.

clue.text: Peculiar game

definitions.meaning: informal British for odd or strange
a card game of melding sets and runs

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for odd, and also names a well-known card game.

clue.text: Disorganised intestate that's the stuff!

indicators.note: disorganised says the letters of the next word are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A will-less estate in a mess, with an exclamation of approval tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorganised' rearranges INTESTATE. 'Stuff' here is cloth, not things in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven fabric, and this is a cotton cloth with a satin-like finish.

clue.text: Plastic — one used to some extent in manufacture of statue

indicators.note: used to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A plastic figure serving as part of the making of a statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'manufacture of statue' cannot stand in for the answer; the definition is 'statue', with 'in manufacture of' only linking.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or sacred figure, and a statue is one such representation of a holy person.

clue.text: General is supporting County

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other one

parts.note: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England

explanation.surface: A general statement that something props up a county.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Cornwallis was the British general who surrendered at Yorktown in 1781.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Cornwallis was a British army general in the American War of Independence.

clue.text: City supplying information about gold, rather meagre

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: news is information
or is the heraldic word for gold
lean means thin or meagre

explanation.surface: A city providing slightly thin information about gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louisiana port on the Mississippi is a major American city.

clue.text: Henry at first boycotts technical institute — he's a craftsman

parts.note: to black a firm or goods is to boycott them in a trade dispute
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the name beside it

explanation.surface: A man called Henry starts by refusing to deal with a technical college, and works with his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Though 'Henry at first' leads the clue, its letter goes at the end of the answer; to 'black' something is a British trade-union term for boycotting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith who forges iron is a traditional skilled craftsman.

clue.text: Man was triumphant

definitions.meaning: to man a ship is to staff it, as a team of sailors does
crowed, in its older past-tense form, means exulted in victory

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a verb here; the second sense uses an old past tense of 'crow'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to staff a vessel, and it is also an archaic past tense of crow, meaning exulted.

clue.text: Without children involved can kidnaps appear neat?

parts.note: SP is sine prole, the genealogical abbreviation meaning without issue

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a childless person's kidnapping tin can look tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes SP with CAN and KIDNAPS; SP (sine prole) is the Latin abbreviation in family trees for dying childless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means spotlessly clean and tidy, so it is a synonym for neat.

clue.text: Stamina required visiting Tyrone

parts.note: staying means visiting, as a guest
Tyrone Power was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Stamina is needed to visit the Northern Irish county of Tyrone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyrone looks like the county in Northern Ireland, but it is the actor Tyrone Power.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means endurance, the ability to keep going, so it equals stamina.

clue.text: Procurers have indulgent ladies initially brought in for flirts

indicators.note: brought in says these letters are placed inside the other piece

parts.note: panders are pimps or procurers

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words it follows

explanation.surface: Pimps with permissive women in tow, taken on for flirtation.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who philanders flirts or has casual affairs, so as verbs the two match.

clue.text: Guy attending reception? Not this guy

parts.note: a guy is a rope stay holding a tent or mast steady
an at-home is a party where hosts receive guests in their house

explanation.surface: Is a man going to the party? No, not him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' first means a supporting rope, then a person. An 'at-home' is a reception held in one's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prefers not to go out is the opposite of a person attending a reception.

clue.text: African child following woman around excessively

indicators.note: following puts the child after the rest
around says one piece wraps the other

parts.note: hen is informal, especially Scottish, for a woman
OTT is over the top, meaning excessively
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: An African youngster trailing after a woman who fusses round too much.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dated and now offensive name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa.

clue.text: PM has to ice a cake

indicators.note: to cake is to form into a mass or crust, so the letters are mixed and compacted anew

explanation.surface: A prime minister obliged to put icing on a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cake' rearranges HAS TO ICE A. The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the title of the Irish head of government, equivalent to a prime minister.

clue.text: Left in a hollow to give birth

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the other piece

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a hollow to have a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and other large mammals are said to calve when they give birth to young.

clue.text: Alloy's composite —- that's true

indicators.note: composite means made of mixed parts, so the letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Declaring that an alloy is a mixture of metals, and that it's true.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal friend is true, faithful and constant.

clue.text: Surgery ready for patients —- a proportion dropped in

indicators.note: dropped in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a clinic that is open is ready to see patients
a ratio is a proportion

explanation.surface: A doctor's surgery is open and some of the patients have dropped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surgery' suggests a British GP's consulting room, matching the surface, but it defines an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a surgical procedure, so surgery describes it.

clue.text: Tried noxious concoction as a soporific

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone tried a nasty mixture as a sleeping draught.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing gas is an anaesthetic that dulls and sends patients under, so it acts as a soporific.

clue.text: Gas rising — by no means unknown

parts.note: x is the algebraic symbol for an unknown

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, reads the word upwards

parts.note: none, as in none the wiser, means not at all

explanation.surface: A gas going up, which is in no way unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NONE upwards to give ENON.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a noble gas, an element found in tiny amounts in the air.

clue.text: Call round

explanation.definitionFit: It means to phone someone, and it is also a circle or circular band.

clue.text: Opposed to a drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone against having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is dialect for against, meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Memo circulating in school

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the word is turned back on itself

parts.note: a note is a memo

explanation.surface: A memo being passed around a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' turns NOTE round; Eton is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known English public school.

clue.text: Mother at home bound to be the motivating force

parts.note: ma is mother
in means at home
to spring is to leap or bound

explanation.surface: A mother at home is certain to be the driving force.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively the chief spring of a watch is the main driving force behind anything.

clue.text: Watch daughter becoming one of the best players

parts.note: to see is to watch

explanation.surface: Watching a daughter turn into a top competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: In tournaments such as tennis, the top-ranked entrants are separated in the draw and called seeds.

clue.text: Female relative I scold about mischief, in one case?

parts.note: she is a female person
nan is a grandmother
to nag is to scold

explanation.surface: A woman's grandmother and the speaker nag one another over a bit of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the scold word round. 'Mischief' is usually a mass noun; 'in one case' asks for a single instance of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shenanigan is a single bit of trickery or mischief, the singular of the usual plural.
